facts.fact: Laid out by Willard Small c. 1892 on the bluff beside Highland Light.
Highland Light (1857) was moved 450 ft west in 1996 because the cliff was eroding.
Bartholomew Gosnold named Cape Cod in 1602 after the cod his crew caught there.

current.subject: Highland Light with beams.
current.keep: The lighthouse, which stands on the course.
current.weaknesses: Pale beams vanish on light cards; the tower floats.

concepts.name: Highland Light by Night
concepts.rationale: The tower on its sand bluff in a night-blue roundel, beams sweeping out over the Atlantic.
concepts.symbolism: The light that has watched the links since 1892.
concepts.tradeoffs: Lighthouses are a common coastal mark.

concepts.name: The Namesake Cod
concepts.rationale: An Atlantic cod: the fish that named the Cape the course stands on.
concepts.symbolism: Cape Cod, named for its fish.
concepts.strengths: Witty and rooted in the place.
concepts.tradeoffs: About the Cape more than the course.

recommendation: Concept 1. The lighthouse stands on the course; the night roundel makes it read.
